Women in the United States secured the right to vote nationally when Tennessee ratified the Nineteenth Amendment on August 18, 1920, and the Secretary of State certified ratification on August 26, 1920 [d1,d5,d8]. Earlier, some U.S. states and localities had allowed women to vote, including brief suffrage in New Jersey from 1797 to 1807 and local voting in Revolutionary-era Massachusetts [d3,d6]. Globally, at least 20 countries granted women the vote in national elections before the U.S., with examples including Britain in 1918 (women over 30) and full equality in 1928, Turkey in 1934, and France in 1944 [d2,d10].
